Pītittika (The Triplet on Rapture)
Section on Analysis:
Root Condition.
Dependent on a state accompanied by rapture, a state accompanied by rapture arises by way of root condition—[namely] a state accompanied by rapture.
Dependent on one aggregate, three aggregates [arise]; dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate [arises];

dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates [arise]. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate accompanied by rapture, three aggregates [arise] …pe… dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates [arise].
Dependent on a state accompanied by rapture, a state accompanied by pleasure arises by way of root condition:
dependent on one aggregate accompanied by rapture, three aggregates accompanied by pleasure arise …pe… dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise.
At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate accompanied by rapture, three aggregates accompanied by pleasure arise …pe…
Dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates [arise].
Dependent on a state accompanied by rapture, states accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure arise by way of root condition:
dependent on one aggregate accompanied by rapture, [arise] states accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure.

Three aggregates … [etc. … dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate accompanied by rapture, three aggregates accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure arise … [etc.
… dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise.
Dependent on a state accompanied by pleasure, a state accompanied by pleasure arises by way of root condition:

dependent on one aggregate accompanied by pleasure, two aggregates [arise]; dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises]. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate accompanied by pleasure, two aggregates [arise]; dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises].
Dependent on a state accompanied by pleasure, a state accompanied by rapture arises by way of root condition:
dependent on one aggregate accompanied by pleasure, three aggregates accompanied by rapture arise …pe… dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise.
At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate accompanied by pleasure, three aggregates accompanied by rapture arise …pe…
Dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates [arise].
Dependent on a state accompanied by pleasure, states accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure arise by way of root condition—
dependent on one aggregate accompanied by pleasure, [states] accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure [arise].

Two aggregates; depending on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises]. At the moment of rebirth-linking (*paṭisandhi*), depending on one aggregate accompanied by pleasure, two aggregates accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure arise; depending on two aggregates, one aggregate arises.
Depending on a state accompanied by equanimity, a state accompanied by equanimity arises by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*): [depending on] a state accompanied by equanimity...
Dependent on one aggregate, two aggregates [arise]; dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises]. At the moment of rebirth-linking …pe….
Dependent on states accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure, a state accompanied by rapture arises by way of root condition:
dependent on one aggregate accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure, three aggregates accompanied by rapture [arise] …pe… dependent on two aggregates …pe….

Dependent on two aggregates, [two aggregates arise]. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure, three aggregates accompanied by rapture arise …pe… dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise.
Dependent on a state accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure, a state accompanied by pleasure arises by way of root condition—[dependent on] a state accompanied by rapture and...
Dependent on one aggregate accompanied by pleasure, there arise two aggregates accompanied by pleasure; dependent on two aggregates, there arises one aggregate.
At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure, there arise two aggregates accompanied by pleasure;
dependent on two aggregates, there arises one aggregate.
Dependent on states accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure, states accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure arise by way of root condition:
dependent on one aggregate accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure, two aggregates [arise]; dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate [arises]. At the moment of rebirth-linking...
Dependent on one aggregate accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure, there arise two aggregates accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure;
dependent on two aggregates, there arises one aggregate.
(Object condition, etc.)

Dependent on a state accompanied by rapture (*pītisahagata*), a state accompanied by rapture arises by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*) … predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*) … (*there is none at the moment of rebirth-linking*) … proximity-condition (*anantarapaccaya*) … contiguity-condition (*samanantarapaccaya*) … conascence-condition (*sahajātapaccaya*) … mutuality-condition (*aññamaññapaccaya*) … support-condition (*nissayapaccaya*) … decisive support-condition (*upanissayapaccaya*) … prenascence-condition (*purejātapaccaya*) … (*in the case of prenascence*).
At the moment of rebirth-linking, there is no condition by way of repetition ... (in repetition, there is no resultant); [there is no condition] by way of kamma-condition ...
resultant-condition ... nutriment ... pe ... faculty ... jhāna ... path ... association ... dissociation ...
presence ... absence ... disappearance ... non-disappearance-condition.
In the Pure Conditionality Chapter:
ten in the root condition, ten in the object condition, ten in the predominance condition, and ten each in the proximity, contiguity, conascence, and mutuality conditions.

In all cases— namely, in the conditions of dependence (nissaya), strong-dependence (upanissaya), prenascence (purejāta), repetition (āsevana), kamma, result (vipāka), nutriment (āhāra), faculty (indriya), jhāna, path (magga), association (sampayutta),
dissociation (vippayutta), presence (atthi), absence (natthi), disappearance (vigata), and non-disappearance (avigata)— there are ten [combinations].
Thus should the enumeration for the direct order (anuloma) be counted.

Dependent on one aggregate accompanied by pleasure, there arise three aggregates accompanied by rapture … dependent on two aggregates, there arise two aggregates.

By this method, ten questions are to be expanded. [This applies to] non-resultant (*navipāka*).

1.8.1.3. Positive-Negative Conditions:
Dyads.

With root condition as the basis, there are ten [instances] for non-predominance; ten for non-prenascence; and ten for non-postnascence, non-repetition, non-kamma, non-resultant, and non-dissociation.
The positive-negative method should be enumerated in detail.
This concludes the positive-negative method.
1.8.1.4. Positive Order of the Negative Conditions (Paccayapaccanīyānuloma) Duka:

With the non-root condition (nahetupaccaya), there are ten [instances] for the object condition (ārammaṇa), ten for the proximity condition (anantara), ten for the contiguity condition (samanantara), and [ten each] for the co-nascence (sahajāta) and mutuality (aññamañña) conditions.
In dependence, strong-dependence, prenascence, repetition, kamma, result, nutriment, faculty, jhāna—each of these has all ten [conditions].
In path, there is one; in association, ten; in dissociation, presence, absence, disappearance, and non-disappearance—each of these has all ten.
This is the negative-positive method.

1.8.7. Chapter on Questions (Pañhāvāra) 1.8.7.1. Section on Analysis (Vibhaṅgavāra) – Positive Conditionality (Paccayānuloma)
A state accompanied by rapture is a condition for a state accompanied by rapture by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).
Roots accompanied by rapture are a condition for their associated aggregates (*khandha*) by way of the root-condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking (*paṭisandhi*), those accompanied by rapture...
Roots are related to associated aggregates by way of root-condition.

A state accompanied by rapture is related to a state accompanied by pleasure by way of root-condition: roots accompanied by rapture are related to associated aggregates accompanied by pleasure by way of root-condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking ...
[etc. ... A state accompanied by rapture is related to a state accompanied by both rapture and pleasure by way of root-condition.
Condition: Roots accompanied by rapture (*pītisahagata*) are related to associated aggregates accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure (*sukhasahagata*) by way of root condition.
At the moment of rebirth-linking (*paṭisandhi*) … [etc.

… A state accompanied by pleasure is related to a state accompanied by pleasure … [etc. … to a state accompanied by rapture … [etc. … to a state accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure … [etc. … (Three [sections] based on pleasure.)

A state accompanied by equanimity is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state accompanied by equanimity: roots accompanied by equanimity are a condition, by way of root-condition, for the associated aggregates. At the moment of rebirth-linking ... [etc. ...
States accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure are conditions, by way of root-condition, for a state accompanied by rapture ...
[etc. ... for a state accompanied by pleasure ... [etc. ... and for a state accompanied by both rapture and pleasure: roots accompanied by rapture ... [etc. ... [are a condition].
And [the roots] accompanied by pleasure are related to the aggregates accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure at the moment of rebirth-linking,
etc., by way of the root condition. Object condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*).
A state accompanied by rapture is a condition for a state accompanied by rapture by way of object-condition:
having given a gift with a mind accompanied by rapture, having undertaken the precepts, and having performed the Uposatha duty, one reviews that with a mind accompanied by rapture;
or, having emerged from jhānas accompanied by rapture, having emerged from the Path, or having emerged from the Fruit.
He reviews that with a mind accompanied by rapture (*pītisahagata*). Noble ones review, with a mind accompanied by rapture, the defilements abandoned which were accompanied by rapture;
they review the defilements suppressed; they know the defilements formerly practiced.
They [review] the aggregates accompanied by rapture with a mind accompanied by rapture as impermanent, suffering, and non-self.
They see clearly, they relish, and they delight in it; with that as object, lust accompanied by rapture arises, and wrong view arises.
Taking the aggregates accompanied by rapture as object, aggregates accompanied by rapture arise.
A state accompanied by rapture is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state accompanied by pleasure—[namely] by means of [a state] accompanied by rapture.
Having given a gift with a mind accompanied by pleasure, having undertaken virtue, and having performed the Uposatha observance, one reviews that with a mind accompanied by pleasure.
Having emerged from jhānas accompanied by rapture, having emerged from the Path, and having emerged from the Fruit, one reviews them with a mind accompanied by pleasure.
Noble ones [review] those accompanied by rapture with a mind accompanied by pleasure.
They review abandoned defilements; they review suppressed defilements; they know previously practiced defilements.
They contemplate with insight the aggregates accompanied by rapture as impermanent, suffering, and non-self with a mind accompanied by pleasure;
they relish them and delight in them; taking that as an object, lust accompanied by pleasure arises, as does wrong view.
...arises. Taking the aggregates accompanied by rapture as an object, aggregates accompanied by pleasure arise.
A state accompanied by rapture is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state accompanied by equanimity:

having given a gift with a mind accompanied by rapture, having undertaken the precepts, and having performed the Uposatha duties, one [contemplates] that [object] with a mind accompanied by equanimity.
One reviews with the mind: having emerged from jhānas accompanied by rapture, having emerged from the Path, and having emerged from the Fruit, one reviews that with a mind accompanied by equanimity.
Noble ones review with a mind accompanied by equanimity the defilements abandoned when accompanied by rapture, they review the defilements suppressed, and [the defilements] formerly practiced.
They know the defilements. With a mind accompanied by equanimity, they practice insight into the aggregates accompanied by rapture as impermanent, suffering, and non-self;

they relish them and delight in them. Taking that as an object, lust accompanied by equanimity arises, wrong view arises, doubt arises, and restlessness arises. By means of the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, [one knows] one who possesses a mind accompanied by rapture...

The mind is known; aggregates accompanied by rapture are related to knowledge of the penetration of others' minds, knowledge of recollection of past lives, knowledge of the destination according to deeds, and knowledge of future states, as well as to advertence, by way of object-condition.
Taking aggregates accompanied by rapture as an object, aggregates accompanied by equanimity arise.
A state accompanied by rapture is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure:

having given a gift with a mind accompanied by rapture, having undertaken precepts, and having performed the Uposatha duty, one reviews that with a mind accompanied by both rapture and pleasure; [as are] the jhānas accompanied by rapture.
Having emerged from the [jhāna], having emerged from the path, and having emerged from the fruit,
one reviews it with a mind accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure. Noble ones review, with a mind accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure,
the defilements that were abandoned which were accompanied by rapture, the defilements that were suppressed, and those formerly practiced.

They know the defilements. They practice insight into the aggregates accompanied by rapture as impermanent, suffering, and non-self with a mind accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure; they relish them and delight in them.
Taking that as an object, lust accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure arises, and wrong view arises. Taking the aggregates accompanied by rapture as an object...
Aggregates accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure arise.

A state accompanied by pleasure is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state accompanied by pleasure … a state accompanied by pleasure for a state accompanied by rapture … [and so on] … for a state accompanied by equanimity … [and so on] … for a state accompanied by rapture.
And a state accompanied by pleasure is a condition for a state accompanied by pleasure by way of object-condition:
taking the aggregates accompanied by pleasure as an object, aggregates accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure arise.
A state accompanied by equanimity is a condition for a state accompanied by equanimity by way of object-condition: [taking] that which is accompanied by equanimity...
Having given a gift with a mind accompanied by equanimity, having undertaken moral discipline, and having performed the Uposatha rites, one reviews that with a mind accompanied by equanimity.

Having emerged from a jhāna accompanied by equanimity, having emerged from a path, and having emerged from a fruition, one reviews that with a mind accompanied by equanimity. Noble ones [review] with a mind accompanied by equanimity...
With a mind accompanied by equanimity, they review defilements that have been abandoned, they review defilements that have been suppressed, and they know defilements previously practiced.

With a mind accompanied by equanimity, they insightfully contemplate the aggregates accompanied by equanimity as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; they relish them and delight in them; taking those as an object, [there arises] a mind accompanied by equanimity.
Lust arises, wrong view arises, doubt arises, restlessness arises.

By means of the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, one knows the mind of one possessing a mind accompanied by equanimity. The base of infinite space is a condition, as an object-condition, for the base of infinite consciousness … pe … the base of nothingness is a condition, as an object-condition, for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

Condition: Aggregates accompanied by equanimity are related to the knowledge of the modes of psychic power (*iddhividha-ñāṇa*), the knowledge of others' minds (*cetopariya-ñāṇa*), the knowledge of recollecting past lives (*pubbenivāsānussati-ñāṇa*), the knowledge of the destination according to karma (*yathākammūpaga-ñāṇa*), the knowledge of future states (*anāgataṁsa-ñāṇa*), and to advertence (*āvajjanā*) by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*).
Taking aggregates accompanied by equanimity as an object, aggregates accompanied by equanimity arise.

A state accompanied by equanimity is a condition, by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*), for a state accompanied by rapture … for a state accompanied by pleasure … for a state accompanied by both rapture and pleasure:

having given a gift with a mind accompanied by equanimity, having undertaken the precepts, and having performed the Uposatha duty, one [reviews] that with a mind accompanied by rapture and … [pleasure].

And having emerged from jhānas accompanied by equanimity, having emerged from the path, and having emerged from the fruit, he reviews them with a mind accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure.
The Noble Ones, with a mind accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure, [review] the defilements abandoned while they were accompanied by equanimity.
They review; they review the defilements that have been suppressed; they know the defilements formerly practiced.
With a mind accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure, they insightfully contemplate the aggregates accompanied by equanimity as impermanent, suffering, and non-self;
they relish them and delight in them; taking that as an object, [there arises] a mind accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure.
And lust arises; wrong view arises. Taking as object the aggregates accompanied by equanimity, the aggregates accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure arise.
Phenomena accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure [are related] to a phenomenon accompanied by rapture …pe… to a phenomenon accompanied by pleasure.
A state accompanied by rapture is related to a state accompanied by equanimity by way of object condition:
having given a gift with a mind accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure, having undertaken the precepts, and having performed the Uposatha duty...
[and so on] ... one contemplates the aggregates accompanied by rapture and accompanied by pleasure as impermanent with a mind accompanied by equanimity.
One contemplates [the object] as suffering and as non-self, yet relishes it and delights in it;
